result:
The simulation is complete and verified. Seven files were built from scratch in the workspace:

- **`index.html`** — exact mandated script order (Three.js 0.147.0 + OrbitControls from CDN, then the five local scripts).
- **`person.js`** — hip/shoulder-pivoted limbs, nose for facing, walk/sit animator.
- **`world.js`** — 6-floor transparent building with real 3-unit entrance gap, 4 offices + conference + lounge per floor, full lobby (cafe, bistro, lounges, pit, reception, kiosk, coolers, loiter spots), BFS nav graph, chunky call panels with cached canvas-digit textures.
- **`elevator_logic.js`** — pure 5-state scheduler with SCAN direction handling, capacity spots, door hold/cap, anti-starvation guards, and oldest-call-first idle pick.
- **`elevator.js`** — yellow car, sliding doors, destination buttons, in-car/shaft indicators, thin adapter over the logic.
- **`sim.js`** — lockstep clock (1–600x slider), day/night keyframes, 20 workers + 80 recycled visitors with full daily schedules, plan compilers, substepped render loop, HUD with occupancy slider.
- **`elevator_logic_test.js`** — 8/8 deterministic tests pass.

Debugging surfaced and fixed four real behavioral bugs: unbounded frame deltas skipping door timers (fixed with logic substeps), agents sampling door state too rarely at high speed (adaptive sim substeps), far-floor starvation (oldest-call scheduling + direction reset on turnaround), and a leave-plan re-trigger loop that bounced workers up/down forever (sticky `leaving` flag + exit overshoot guard).

Verification: `node elevator_logic_test.js` 8/8, `static_check` clean, Playwright `runtime_check` nonblank canvas with motion and zero console errors, full-day soaks at 30x–600x show morning rush, meetings, lunch surge, complete evening exodus, clean day wrap, correct seated orientations (38/38 facing checks), and no door bunching.
cost_note: Qoder uses Credits and the CLI does not report per-run USD cost
